key_insight: A physics-constrained statistical framework infers latent molar mass and Debye temperature from energy and pressure data while guaranteeing thermodynamic consistency by construction.
engineering_relevance: The approach reduces reliance on material-specific hand-tuning when building equations of state for hydrodynamic simulations of dissociative materials.
method: Infer latent physical quantities from internal energy and pressure, which are derivatives of free energy.
Represent local molar-mass behavior with polynomial bases across domain partitions.
Model Debye temperature with an I-spline basis and quantify inference uncertainty.
evidence_signal: Simulations and a carbon dioxide case study show accurate recovery of underlying physical quantities, improved held-out energy and pressure predictions, and scaling with EOS table size.
watch_item: Validation beyond carbon dioxide remains to be established, particularly across materials with different dissociation behavior.
paper_title: Physics-Constrained Modeling and Inference of the Equation of State for Dissociative Materials
